summary.one_liner: Maige is an AI-driven GitHub helper that manages issue labels and other repo maintenance tasks through a GitHub App integration.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Maige as a tool for repo maintenance, where AI handles issue labels after setup. It is operated through a hosted service at Maige.app. Users interact with it by opening issues and giving natural-language commands such as assigning yourself to an issue, removing all labels, adding a label when a keyword appears, or asking what packages a repo uses. It works via a GitHub App that receives webhooks for issues, issue comments, and pull requests. The README also covers a self-hosted setup path using Bun, environment variables, and ngrok, but notes that self-hosting is not yet supported.
use_cases: automatically label GitHub issues with AI
triage new issues in a repository
bulk remove labels from an issue
auto-apply labels when keywords appear in issues
ask questions about a repo's packages from an issue
how_to_run: Create a GitHub App with Issue and Pull Request read/write permissions and issues, issue comments, and pull requests events, then add its credentials to .env
notable: Natural-language commands given directly in GitHub issues
Runs as a GitHub App using webhooks
Environment secrets managed via Infisical CLI
caveats: Self-hosting is explicitly not yet supported per the README
Requires creating and configuring a GitHub App with webhook and ngrok tunneling for local use
Setup involves multiple secrets (webhook secret, private key conversion)
